title: A Promise Made to an Unknown Reader
title_ja: まだ見ぬ読者への約束
fact_notes: 人物・出来事・制度・任務は架空の教材例。実在の調査・統計・実証結果・宇宙運用基準や法令ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: Imagine a fictional student newspaper collecting articles about the experiences of people who have participated in a community project over the past several years.
sentences.ja: 過去数年に地域活動に参加した人々の経験について記事を集める架空の生徒新聞を想像しよう。

sentences.en: The editors hope to preserve these accounts in a digital archive so that future students will be able to learn about the development of the project.
sentences.ja: 将来の生徒が活動の発展を学べるよう記述をデジタル資料庫に保存したいと編集者は考える。

sentences.en: Several contributors agree to publication because they expect the articles to be read primarily by members of their own school community.
sentences.ja: 記事は主に学校共同体のメンバーに読まれると期待して掲載に同意する寄稿者もいる。

sentences.en: The editors subsequently realize that making the archive available through a public website could expose the same accounts to a much wider and less predictable audience.
sentences.ja: その後公開ウェブサイトを通じ資料を閲覧可能にすると同じ記述がはるかに広く予測しにくい読者にさらされ得ると気づく。

sentences.en: One student argues that obtaining permission to publish an article should be sufficient, since the contributors have already agreed to let other people read their words.
sentences.ja: 寄稿者は他者が言葉を読むことに既に同意したので掲載許可で十分だと一人の生徒は主張する。

sentences.en: Another points out that the significance of a disclosure may depend on who receives the information and how easily it can be connected with other available material.
sentences.ja: 情報公開の意味は誰が受け取るか、他の資料とどれほど容易に関連づけられるかに依存し得ると別の生徒が指摘する。

sentences.en: A detail that appears entirely ordinary within a familiar community could acquire a different meaning when encountered by someone who lacks the relevant context.
sentences.ja: 身近な共同体では普通に見える詳細も関連文脈のない人が触れると別の意味を持ち得る。

sentences.en: The disagreement encourages the editors to distinguish permission for a particular form of publication from a general agreement to every possible future use of the material.
sentences.ja: 対立は特定形態の掲載許可と将来のあらゆる利用への一般同意を区別するよう促す。

sentences.en: The students examine several possible designs for the archive rather than treating a fully public collection as the only way to preserve the project's history.
sentences.ja: 完全公開だけを活動史の保存方法と考えず複数の資料庫設計を検討する。

sentences.en: Some materials could be made publicly accessible, while other accounts might be retained within a restricted collection intended for a more clearly defined audience.
sentences.ja: 一部は一般公開でき、他の記述はより明確な読者を対象とする制限付き資料に残せるかもしれない。

sentences.en: They also consider publishing summaries that describe significant developments without reproducing potentially identifying details that are unnecessary for understanding the wider project.
sentences.ja: 大きな活動を理解する上で不要な個人特定につながり得る詳細を再掲せず重要な変化を説明する要約の公開も検討する。

sentences.en: The editors recognize that merely removing a person's name cannot guarantee anonymity if the remaining details make that individual readily recognizable to a particular audience.
sentences.ja: 残る詳細で特定読者が人物を容易に認識できれば名前を除くだけでは匿名性を保証できないと認識する。

sentences.en: Before changing the form of publication, the editors decide to explain the proposed arrangements to the contributors and invite them to consider the new conditions.
sentences.ja: 掲載形態を変える前に提案を寄稿者に説明し新条件を検討するよう求めることにする。

sentences.en: They acknowledge that some people may no longer be available for consultation and that the absence of a response cannot automatically be interpreted as agreement.
sentences.ja: 相談できない人もおり応答がないことを自動的に同意と解釈できないと認める。

sentences.en: For accounts whose status remains uncertain, they consider alternative ways of documenting the history without extending access to the original personal material.
sentences.ja: 位置づけが不確かな記述では元の個人的資料へのアクセスを広げず歴史を記録する別の方法を考える。

sentences.en: The fictional exercise does not establish a legal rule about publication or data protection; its purpose is to explore the ethical relationship between communication and the expectations under which information was supplied.
sentences.ja: 架空の活動は掲載やデータ保護についての法的規則を確立せず、伝達と情報提供時の期待の倫理的関係を考えることが目的だ。

sentences.en: The example illustrates that the preservation of information and the expansion of access to it are related but distinct decisions.
sentences.ja: 情報保存とアクセス拡大は関係するが異なる判断だと例は示す。

sentences.en: A valuable record may deserve protection without necessarily being suitable for distribution to every audience through every available medium.
sentences.ja: 価値ある記録は守るに値してもあらゆる媒体で全読者へ配布するのに適するとは限らない。

sentences.en: Responsible publication requires attention not only to the benefits that future readers might obtain but also to the circumstances in which the people represented in the material agreed to contribute.
sentences.ja: 責任ある掲載には将来の読者の利益だけでなく資料に表れる人々が提供に同意した事情への注意が必要だ。

sentences.en: The editors learn that serving an unknown future audience does not require forgetting the commitments that made it possible to collect the information in the first place.
sentences.ja: まだ見ぬ将来の読者に奉仕するため最初に情報収集を可能にした約束を忘れる必要はないと編集者は学ぶ。

able to be reached or used
state of identity not being known

questions.prompt: What do the editors want to preserve?
options: The history of a distant planet.

questions.prompt: Why might public access change the situation?
options: The audience could become wider and less predictable.

questions.prompt: What does one student consider sufficient?
Why distinguish types of publication permission?
options: Context and audience can change the implications of disclosure.
Contributors always permit every possible use.
questions.explanation_ja: 文脈・読者で意味が変わる。

options: Allowing only future students to write.

questions.prompt: Why might removing names not guarantee anonymity?
questions.explanation_ja: 残る情報から特定可能。

questions.prompt: What do editors plan before changing publication?
options: Explain new arrangements and consult contributors.

questions.prompt: Why consider alternatives when consent is unclear?
options: Assume missing responses are permanent agreements.
Preserve history without unnecessarily extending access to personal material.
Prove the legal status of every record.
Exclude all future readers from history.
questions.explanation_ja: 保存とアクセスを区別。

options: All historical records must be publicly accessible.
Permission to publish means unlimited future use.
Preserving information and widening access should respect the context of contributors' agreement.
Future readers have no interest in archives.
questions.explanation_ja: 情報提供時の合意を尊重。

paraphrases.source: The editors hope to preserve these accounts in a digital archive so that future students will be able to learn about the development of the project.
paraphrases.rewrite: They plan to preserve accounts for future students to understand the project.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 将来の学習のため保存。

paraphrases.source: Another points out that the significance of a disclosure may depend on who receives the information and how easily it can be connected with other available material.
paraphrases.rewrite: The effects of disclosure depend partly on who sees it and links it to other information.

paraphrases.source: The editors recognize that merely removing a person's name cannot guarantee anonymity if the remaining details make that individual readily recognizable to a particular audience.
paraphrases.rewrite: Removing names cannot ensure anonymity when other details reveal identity.

paraphrases.source: Responsible publication requires attention not only to the benefits that future readers might obtain but also to the circumstances in which the people represented in the material agreed to contribute.
paraphrases.rewrite: Publication should consider both future readers' benefits and contributors' expectations when they agreed to share.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 読者の利益と提供時の事情。
